is the squared residual--probe correlation, i.e.\ the fraction of residual

issues.failure_explanation: Even when the probe has empirical mean zero and variance one, the numerator is the squared empirical covariance, but the denominator is the uncentered residual second moment rather than the empirical residual variance. Thus the formula is not the squared residual–probe correlation unless the diagnostic residual has exactly zero empirical mean. As written it instead gives the fraction of residual mean-square removed by adding that single probe.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Center the residuals in the denominator, or consistently describe the quantity as the fraction of uncentered residual mean-square removed rather than a squared correlation or fraction of residual variance.
issues.overall_effect: The effect-size interpretation used in the stopping procedure, taxonomy, and numerical demonstrations is not exact for finite diagnostic samples with nonzero mean residual.
issues.title: The stated effect size is not generally a squared correlation
issues.why_classification: A short local change to the denominator or terminology restores the claimed interpretation without changing the method or its substantive scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
These conditions license reading
$\hat\sigma_r^2$ as the estimated aleatoric floor $\E[\Var(Y\mid X)]$.

Step~3
guards against it by phrasing the barrier as an \emph{equivalence}-style
statement (no out-of-basis direction removes more than $\varepsilon$ of the
residual variance) that must remain \emph{stable} as the probe family is
enriched, rather than as a single passing test.

issues.failure_explanation: The population characterization requires orthogonality to every square-integrable function of X, whereas the procedure examines only finitely many selected probes and supplies no structural assumption or uniform error bound controlling untested directions. Moreover, bounding the maximum effect of individual probes does not bound their aggregate effect: a residual signal can be distributed over many orthogonal probes so that every individual effect is at most ε while a linear combination explains a large fraction of the residual. Stability over an empirically chosen finite enrichment schedule does not rule this out. Consequently the stop rule cannot certify that the approximation gap is negligible or that the observed residual mean-square is the aleatoric floor.

failure_location.quote:
Across the schedule, declare the barrier reached when
no out-of-basis probe is both significant \emph{and} practically
large---operationally, when $\max_\psi e_n(\psi)\le\varepsilon$ for a task-set
tolerance $\varepsilon$ fixed independently of $n$---and when enriching the
family further no longer reduces $\hat\sigma_r^2$ beyond sampling noise.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either weaken all certification and floor-identification claims to explicitly heuristic evidence, or impose a controlled residual function class and provide aggregate, uniform finite-sample bounds over that class.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised finite-data identification of Regimes II and III, including the claimed inference that the Lorenz–96 degree-3 residual estimates the irreducible conditional variance, is unsupported. The procedure remains a heuristic specification check but not a certificate that deterministic improvement is impossible.
issues.title: Finite probe checks cannot certify the conditional-mean barrier
issues.why_classification: A rigorous repair requires new statistical assumptions and proof architecture, while the direct source-supported alternative withdraws the paper's central promise that the finite-data procedure locates and certifies the conditional-mean barrier.

issues.failure_explanation: Square integrability permits Y to be almost surely constant, in which case Var(Y)=0. The definition and ceiling formulas then divide by zero, and the asserted value in [0,1] is not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume Var(Y)>0 throughout the R² subsection and handle constant Y separately.
issues.overall_effect: The R² definition and ceiling discussion do not cover the degenerate output laws allowed by the paper's standing assumptions.
issues.title: The coefficient of determination is undefined for constant outputs
issues.why_classification: A standard local nondegeneracy condition resolves the boundary case without changing any nondegenerate conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The algebra separates the cross-entropy into KL divergence plus differential entropy without assuming that the relevant positive and negative parts are integrable. For densities with non-finite or undefined differential entropy, this separation can involve an undefined infinity subtraction, so the displayed identity and the ensuing optimization equivalence do not follow as written.
